run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The P1 alert (onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease, workload clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks) could not be tied to anything observable in the connected environment. Only two Elasticsearch indices exist (app-235-change-history, app-235-cluster-inventory), and the three in-window change-history rows describe jenkins, argocd-server and gitlab-runner in namespace ci on cluster ci-cd; the connected cluster lists 8 namespaces (app-162, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo) and none of those ci workloads exists, so the inventory/change rows do not describe objects in the cluster I could inspect. The most recent in-window change is 07:39:05Z (gitlab-runner scale 2 to 3), about 90 minutes before the alert's ~09:09 start, so the premise 'alert started right after a deployment' is not supported by the available change data. Separately, I found a real but temporally later fault in namespace app-162: the payments-service deployment (created 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z) logs 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', its /ready and /health return 503, it was restarted once after a failed liveness probe (exit code 137), its ClusterIP service has no endpoints, and the two signup-service pods fail readiness with Connection refused to payments-service. That chain began ~29 minutes after the alert's start and no evidence ties it to the clientorg-alpha online-devices alert. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable throughout this Run, so no metric, label or span evidence (including any online-device count) could be examined.

claims.text: The registered Elasticsearch target holds only two indices: app-235-change-history (4 documents) and app-235-cluster-inventory (6 documents).

Inside the authorized window (2026-11-21T09:39:18Z to 2026-11-22T09:39:18Z) app-235-change-history returns exactly 3 rows: jenkins deployment to 2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-22T03:39:05Z, argocd-server deployment to v2.9.3 at 2026-11-22T04:39:05Z, and a gitlab-runner scale from 2 to 3 replicas at 2026-11-22T07:39:05Z; all have cluster ci-cd and namespace ci, and none mentions clientorg-alpha or lambda-dashboard-monitoring.

Inside the same window app-235-cluster-inventory returns exactly 3 rows for cluster ci-cd namespace ci: gitlab-runner (gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0, 3 replicas, Running), jenkins (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts, 1 replica, Running) and argocd-server (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3, 2 replicas, Running).

The cluster has 8 namespaces: app-162, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; there is no namespace ci and no namespace or object carrying the alert's org/workload name clientorg-alpha.

A full all-namespace listing (35 pods, 26 deployments, neither truncated) contains no jenkins, argocd-server or gitlab-runner workload, and no pod or deployment named for clientorg-alpha or lambda-dashboard-monitoring; apart from the app-162 pods started 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z, pod start times are 2026-11-20T16:3x/16:32 or 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z, so no workload rollout is visible between 09:00Z and 09:38Z.

In kube-system the static control-plane pods etcd-opspilot-m1-control-plane, kube-apiserver-opspilot-m1-control-plane, kube-controller-manager-opspilot-m1-control-plane and kube-scheduler-opspilot-m1-control-plane show startTime 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z and restart counts 1-2.

Deployments app-162/payments-service (replicas 1) and app-162/signup-service (replicas 2) were both created at 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z at deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, and their only ReplicaSets payments-service-6d94c44fdc and signup-service-7c89545dc9 were created at 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z, i.e. no earlier revision of either workload is visible.

Pod app-162/payments-service-6d94c44fdc-npkjt has Ready=False (ContainersNotReady), restartCount 1, and lastState terminated with exitCode 137, reason Error, startedAt 2026-11-22T09:38:20Z and finishedAt 2026-11-22T09:39:20Z.

payments-service container logs contain the exact lines 'ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', 'ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', and repeated 'GET /ready' and 'GET /health' 503 responses between 2026-11-22T09:38:22Z and 2026-11-22T09:39:15Z.
A Normal event on Pod app-162/payments-service-6d94c44fdc-npkjt at 2026-11-22T09:38:50Z reads 'Container payments-service failed liveness probe, will be restarted' (reason Killing).

Pod app-162/signup-service-7c89545dc9-6xjkz is Ready=False (ContainersNotReady) with restartCount 0, and its logs repeatedly show 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' with GET /ready returning 503 while GET /health returns 200.

Endpoints objects app-162/payments-service and app-162/signup-service both have no addresses and no not-ready addresses, which matches the connection refusals seen by signup-service against http://payments-service:8080.

Warning events in the window include 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-95/orca: endpoints "orca" already exists' at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z and 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-162/signup-service: endpoints "signup-service" already exists' at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z; no namespace app-95 exists in the current namespace listing.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap declares fault flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad with defaultVariant 'off' in every case (state ENABLED only means the flag definition is loaded).

The user's premise that the alert started right after a deployment is not supported by the change data: the newest in-window change is the gitlab-runner scale at 2026-11-22T07:39:05Z, roughly 90 minutes before the alert's ~09:09:18Z start, and it targets namespace ci on cluster ci-cd, which has no deployment or pod in the connected cluster; no rollout is visible in pod start times between 09:00Z and 09:38Z.

The P1 alert belongs to a different monitored environment than the one queried here (its labels name cluster us-prod-eks, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring and workload clientorg-alpha, while the queried target is the kind cluster opspilot-m1-control-plane holding otel-demo and app-162, and its inventory rows describe cluster ci-cd), so its cause is not contained in the available evidence.

For app-162 the failure chain is: the Stripe key supplied to payments-service (env STRIPE_API_KEY from Secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key, which also provides the app-code volume) is invalid, so /ready and /health answer 503, the liveness probe kills the container (exit 137), the payments-service ClusterIP has no ready endpoints, and signup-service readiness checks to http://payments-service:8080 get Connection refused; this began at 2026-11-22T09:38:19Z, about 29 minutes after the alert start, and no evidence ties it to the clientorg-alpha online-devices alert.

Rejected: the gitlab-runner scale-up (2 to 3 replicas at 2026-11-22T07:39:05Z) as the cause of the P1 alert - the workload, its namespace ci and cluster ci-cd appear nowhere in the queried cluster's 26 deployments or 35 pods, and the change predates the alert start by about 90 minutes.

Rejected: the otel-demo flagd fault-injection flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure and the others) as the cause of the app-162 payment failure - every flag in flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off', and the failing component is app-162/payments-service, a separate workload from otel-demo/payment.

Get telemetry for the alert's own environment (cluster us-prod-eks, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha): the online-device trend cannot be evaluated from this target, and the alert claims an 8-hour gradual decline that no deployment in this cluster can explain.

For app-162, have a human verify and correct the stripe-api-key value in Secret payments-secrets (and the app-code entries in that same Secret), then recreate payments-service so its liveness/readiness probes pass; signup-service readiness depends on payments-service having endpoints. Secrets cannot be read by this investigation, so the value was not verified.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole Run: get_label_values for service_name (twice), execute_prometheus_instant_query (count(up), up, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-162"}), get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (one instant query also returned INVALID_PARAMS). No metric or label series could be examined, so any online-device count, error rate or availability signal is unknown, not zero; the metric names that could have shown it are app_payment_transactions_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket/count, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace,deployment}.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on both attempts, so no spans, error status codes or caller-callee edges could be checked.

The alert's own subject is missing from every available source: no Kubernetes object, no change-history row and no inventory row carries clientorg-alpha, lambda-dashboard-monitoring or cluster us-prod-eks; a change_history integration is listed as not integrated, and only the app-235-change-history Elasticsearch index was available.

Both indices hold documents outside the authorized window that cannot be read because the Elasticsearch time filter cannot be turned off (app-235-change-history has 4 documents but 3 in-window rows; app-235-cluster-inventory has 6 documents but 3 in-window rows), so any older change is unknown.
Secrets payments-secrets and signup-secrets could not be read, so the actual stripe-api-key and database-url values are unverified; the invalid-key conclusion rests on the container's own log text.

Namespace app-95 and service orca are referenced by a 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z FailedToCreateEndpoint warning but no app-95 namespace or object exists now, so that object is unreadable and its relationship to the alert is unknown.

No event was returned between the alert's ~09:09:18Z start and the first in-window event at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z, so what happened at alert onset is unobserved; 7 events fell outside the authorized window and were dropped.

The kube-system static pods etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler show startTime 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z with restart counts 1-2 during the incident window; nothing in the evidence explains that restart, so it is recorded as an unexplained change, not as impact.

Kubernetes objects show only their state at query time (about 2026-11-22T09:39-09:40Z); the cluster state at the alert start (~09:09Z) is unknown, and the deployment/ReplicaSet/pod creation times for app-162 are the only rollout history visible.
next_steps: Pull the Grafana/lambda-dashboard-monitoring telemetry for clientorg-alpha on us-prod-eks (online-devices count, its 8-hour history and the deployment/change feed of that cluster) to find what changed near 09:09Z.

Have a human read Secret payments-secrets in app-162 and confirm the stripe-api-key and app-code values, then roll payments-service after correcting them; expect signup-service readiness to recover once payments-service has endpoints.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger reachability for this target so the app-162 payment signals and any error-rate or latency baselines can be checked directly.
Check the deleted app-95/orca service history and the 08:04Z control-plane pod restart in kube-system to rule them out as unrelated changes.

    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self

  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
